actor_report:
Observations: ISSUE_9.md says page_count(11, 10) returns 1 but should return 2. The owner classifies the issue as trivial-fix and authorises a direct change to utils/paging.py with a regression test in tests/test_paging.py. POLICY.md lets the implementing actor make and close trivial-fix changes without separate review, so no independent review is required (TICKET_METHOD STDO-UP-007). The cause is in utils/paging.py: `total // per_page` is floor division, so a partial final page is dropped.

Work: I replaced floor division with ceiling division, `-(-total // per_page)`. The per_page validation is unchanged. I added two regression tests: page_count(11, 10) == 2 and page_count(1, 10) == 1. The existing tests are unchanged. By inspection, they still hold under the new code: 20/10 -> 2 and 0/10 -> 0. The edits stay within the two files named in the grant (RF-006).

What this report does not establish:
(1) I had no execution capability, so no tests were run. Whether the tests pass is still undecided (FOUNDATIONS Result algebra: not_performed -> indeterminate). The host's assertion run is the evidence that would decide it.
(2) The edits are proposals only. The host applies them, so the file-change effect is not_started from my side.
(3) Closure of issue 9 is not claimed. The policy permits the implementing actor to close the issue, but closure requires its obligations to be satisfied (TICKET_METHOD Condition-Based Closure), and the test result is still undecided.
(4) Negative total is outside the issue's scope and its expected behaviour is unspecified. Its result changes: page_count(-5, 10) used to return -1 and now returns 0. I added no test or validation for it. If it matters, the owner should decide the intended behaviour (SPEC_METHOD Computed Classification: residual judgment J / owner ruling O).
